ai.literal: He hoarded - at the place of - abundant - great wealth - that - he does not enjoy - he is dead - to do - remained - nothing.
ai.translation: He who hoards vast wealth but does not enjoy it is as good as dead. There is nothing left for him to do.
ai.modern: தன்னிடம் நிறைய செல்வத்தை சேர்த்து வைத்தும் அதனை அனுபவிக்காதவன் இறந்தவனுக்குச் சமமாவான். அவனால் செய்யக்கூடியது வேறு ஒன்றும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the ultimate uselessness of wealth when it is merely hoarded. The word 'வைத்தான்' refers to one who just keeps or hoards wealth, while 'உண்ணான்' means he does not consume or enjoy it. The poet boldly declares such a person 'செத்தான்' (dead), because without using his wealth for himself or others, his existence has no purpose or remaining potential ('செயக்கிடந்தது இல்').

ai.literal: by wealth / will happen / everything / thinking that / not giving / hoarding / from delusion / results / unexcellent / birth
ai.translation: From the delusion of hoarding wealth without giving, thinking that everything is achieved through it, results a wretched birth.
ai.modern: பொருளால் எல்லாம் நடக்கும் என்று நினைத்து, யாருக்கும் எதையும் கொடுக்காமல் சேர்த்து வைக்கும் மயக்கத்தால், ஒருவனுக்குச் சிறப்பற்ற பிறவி உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet warns against the obsessive accumulation of wealth. It describes a person who believes that money can accomplish absolutely everything, leading them to hoard it without giving anything to others. This mindset is termed a 'delusion' (மருள்). The consequence of such a deluded, miserly life is an 'inglorious birth' (மாணாப் பிறப்பு), meaning a wretched and miserable existence.

ai.literal: accumulation hoarding fame not-desiring men appearance to-earth burden
ai.translation: The existence of men who hoard their wealth and do not desire fame is a mere burden to the earth.
ai.modern: பொருளைச் சேர்த்து வைத்து யாருக்கும் கொடுக்காமல் புகழை விரும்பாத மனிதர்களின் பிறப்பு, இந்தப் பூமிக்கு ஒரு சுமையே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet condemns those who accumulate wealth only to hoard it, showing no desire for the good fame that comes from generosity. The word 'இவறி' means holding on tightly or being miserly with one's accumulation ('ஈட்டம்'). The poet declares that the very existence ('தோற்றம்') of such men serves no purpose and is nothing but a dead weight ('பொறை') upon the earth.

ai.literal: Legacy saying what will think indeed by anyone to desire he who is not subjected.
ai.translation: What will he think of as his legacy, the man who is not desired by anyone?
ai.modern: ஒருவராலும் விரும்பப்படாதவன், தனக்குப் பின் எஞ்சி நிற்பது என்று எதை நினைப்பானோ?
ai.explanation: A person who hoards wealth without helping others is not loved or sought after by anyone. When such a person reflects on his life, he will find nothing of value to leave behind. The word eccam refers to what remains after one is gone, such as descendants or a good name, which the unloved miser entirely lacks.

words.gloss: to those who do not have

ai.literal: Giving and enjoying, to those who do not have, piled up ten million exists even if, nothing.
ai.translation: For those who neither give to others nor enjoy it themselves, even if they possess ten million piled up, it is nothing.
ai.modern: பிறருக்குக் கொடுப்பதும் தான் அனுபவிப்பதும் இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு, பல கோடிகள் சேர்ந்திருந்தாலும் அதனால் ஒரு பயனும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the true purpose of wealth, which is to be shared with others and enjoyed by oneself. The elongated words 'கொடுப்பதூஉம்' (giving) and 'துய்ப்பதூஉம்' (enjoying) emphasize these two essential actions. If a person lacks the heart to do either, their wealth is entirely useless, even if they have amassed millions.

ai.literal: A burden is great wealth for him who himself does not enjoy, to the worthy anything giving nature he who does not have.
ai.translation: Vast wealth is merely a burden to the man who neither enjoys it himself nor has the nature of giving anything to the worthy.
ai.modern: தான் அனுபவிக்காமலும், தகுதியுடையவர்களுக்கு ஒன்றையும் கொடுக்கும் குணம் இல்லாமலும் இருப்பவனுக்கு அவனது பெரும் செல்வம் ஒரு சுமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the futility of hoarding wealth without using it. The word etam means a burden, affliction, or disease, showing that unused wealth is not a blessing but a curse. The hoarder is described as someone who neither consumes the wealth himself nor possesses the natural inclination to give to deserving people. Thus, wealth without utility or charity becomes a heavy, useless load on its possessor.

ai.literal: To the destitute anything he who does not give wealth, great beauty she who obtained solitary woman having aged is like that.
ai.translation: The wealth of a man who gives nothing to the destitute is like a woman of great beauty growing old in loneliness.
ai.modern: வறியவர்களுக்கு ஒரு சிறு பொருளையும் கொடுத்து உதவாதவனுடைய செல்வமானது, மிகுந்த அழகைப் பெற்ற ஒரு பெண் தனிமையிலேயே வாழ்ந்து முதுமை அடைவதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares hoarded, unused wealth to unshared beauty. The word 'அற்றார்க்கு' refers to those who are destitute or lack resources, while 'ஆற்றாதான்' denotes a person who fails to do the duty of giving. The wealth of such a miser is likened to a woman of great beauty ('மிக நலம் பெற்றாள்') who grows old entirely alone ('தமியள் மூத்து'). Just as her beauty fades without ever being appreciated or bringing joy to a partner, the miser's wealth is wasted because it never brings relief to those in need or joy to the giver.

ai.literal: To desire - he who is not experienced - wealth - middle - inside town - poison - tree - having ripened - it is like.
ai.translation: The wealth of a man whom no one loves is like a poisonous tree bearing fruit in the middle of a town.
ai.modern: யாராலும் விரும்பப்படாதவனுடைய செல்வம், ஊரின் நடுவே உள்ள ஒரு நச்சுமரம் பழுத்ததைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the wealth of an unloved, miserly person to a poisonous tree fruiting in the center of a town. 'நச்சப் படாதவன்' refers to one who is not desired or loved by others, usually because he does not help anyone. Even though his 'செல்வம்' (wealth) is abundant and accessible, like a tree in the 'நடு ஊருள்' (middle of the town), it is utterly useless and even harmful, just as the fruits of a 'நச்சு மரம்' (poisonous tree) cannot be eaten. The wealth benefits no one and only causes sorrow.

ai.literal: Love having shunned, oneself having afflicted, virtue without considering, accumulated bright wealth, will take others.
ai.translation: Strangers will seize the brilliant wealth accumulated by one who shuns love, starves oneself, and ignores virtue.
ai.modern: அன்பை விலக்கி, தன்னையும் வருத்திக்கொண்டு, அறத்தையும் செய்யாமல் ஒருவன் சேர்த்த சிறந்த செல்வத்தை மற்றவர்களே எடுத்துக்கொள்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the ultimate fate of wealth hoarded by a miser. Such a person abandons love for family and friends, denies themselves basic comforts, and refuses to perform charitable deeds. Because they merely accumulate this brilliant wealth without using it, it will eventually fall into the hands of strangers.

ai.literal: Excellence possessing wealthy people's small distress, rain cloud drought having become intense like that it possesses.
ai.translation: When wealthy people of excellent character suffer a brief period of poverty, it is as devastating to the world as a rain cloud failing in a severe drought.
ai.modern: சிறந்த பண்புடைய செல்வர்கள் சிறிது வறுமை அடைவது, மழைமேகம் வறண்டு போவதைப் போன்ற தன்மையை உடையது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the wealth of the generous with the useless wealth discussed in this chapter. The word 'cīr' refers to the excellence of a generous character, while 'tuṉi' means distress or poverty. When such noble people experience even a brief period of poverty, the world feels the loss deeply. The poet compares this to a rain cloud ('māri') becoming dry ('vaṟam'), showing that just as all life depends on rain, many depend on the generous wealthy.
